slides.headline: BUILD YOUR OWN CHATGPT IN 6 STEPS, DEPLOYED WITH REAL USERS
slides.kicker: DO IT ALONE AND LEARN EVERYTHING
slides.image_prompt: Sam Altman waist-up, yellow hard hat, triumphant grin, holding circuit blueprint, bright amber workshop, three glowing stations, white OpenAI logo on wall, electric blue accent, sharp documentary 35mm film grain.

slides.headline: 1) RUN YOUR OWN AI MODEL THE WAY CHATGPT DOES
slides.body:
Every time ChatGPT answers you, a machine runs a model on a server. Now you build that setup.

Take a free AI model. Load it into a serving tool. Give it a web address

slides.headline: 2) ADD USERS, LOGIN, AND MEMORY TO YOUR AI
slides.body:
A bare AI has no memory. Every session starts fresh. Add this and it becomes a product.

Set up a database. Build user login. Store conversations. Now 100 people can use it at once

slides.headline: 3) BUILD THE CHAT WINDOW USERS ACTUALLY TOUCH
slides.body:
The backend runs hidden. The chat window is what users actually see and touch.

Build a simple page. Users type messages. The AI responds in real time. Chat history loads on return

slides.headline: 4) TEACH YOUR AI TO READ YOUR OWN FILES
slides.body:
A default AI knows nothing about your business. This step fixes that.

Load your documents in. Build a search layer. The AI reads your files before it answers anything
slides.image_prompt: Hands fanning a stack of glowing papers toward a laptop screen, a magnifying glass symbol extracting highlighted passages from the pages — no text — vivid teal backdrop; accent: bright orange against teal. Documentary news photo, 35mm, harsh on-camera flash, film grain.

slides.headline: 5) GIVE YOUR AI THE POWER TO TAKE REAL ACTIONS
slides.body:
Reading is one thing. Doing is another. Here your AI stops giving answers and starts taking steps.

Connect it to search, calendars, and live data. It picks which tool to use on its own
slides.image_prompt: Close laptop screen: a glowing hub circle with electric blue arrows branching to a search magnifying glass, calendar symbol, and database cylinder — bright checkmarks on each branch — vivid lime backdrop; accent: electric blue against lime. Documentary news photo, 35mm, harsh on-camera flash, film grain.

slides.headline: 6) DEPLOY YOUR AI AND TEST WITH REAL TRAFFIC
slides.body:
This is where practice becomes a real product. Send 100 users at once and see what breaks.

Run it on a cloud server. Package it in a container. Send real traffic. Fix what cracks

slides.headline: SAVE THIS: 6 STEPS TO BUILD YOUR OWN AI
slides.body:
1. Run it on a server
2. Add users and memory
3. Give it your documents
4. Give it power to act
5. Deploy and test for real

Daily AI news + real skills

caption:
Swipe through all 6. These are the exact steps serious AI builders take when learning how to do it for real. 🔧

Run your own AI server from zero, then add user accounts, login, and conversation memory, then build the chat interface users actually see and touch, then give the AI access to your own documents, then connect it to live tools so it can take real actions, then deploy the whole system and test it under real traffic.

Most people learn AI by watching tutorials. The builders who actually ship things learn by doing this project alone. The gap between those two groups is growing. Running a business? DM us "AI" and we'll show you what this could do for yours.

Sources: karancl
